title: Webhook receives data but no active scenario is listening
problem: An event is sent to a Make webhook URL, but no active scenario is listening on that webhook. Make does not process the payload. The sending service may receive a non-200 response or a queued acknowledgment.
symptoms: External service logs show the webhook request was sent but no scenario executed in Make
Make webhook shows received payloads in its queue with no corresponding executions
Scenario history is empty despite events being dispatched

likely_causes.cause: The scenario using this webhook is inactive — Make requires the scenario to be active to process incoming webhook data
The webhook URL registered in the external service points to a deleted or recreated Make webhook with a different URL

diagnosis_steps: Verify the scenario is active — the scenario toggle must be ON
Open Make > Webhooks and confirm the webhook shows as 'Listening'
Compare the webhook URL configured in the external service with the current URL shown in Make
Send a test event and use 'Run once' to verify reception in real time

solutions.solution: Activate the scenario by turning the scenario toggle to ON
Update the webhook URL in the external service to match the current Make webhook URL
solutions.conditions: When the URL in the external service is outdated

prevention: Always activate the scenario before registering the webhook URL in an external service
Document the webhook URL alongside which external service uses it — regenerating the webhook invalidates the URL

origin_details.evidence: Make requires the scenario to be active for the webhook trigger to process incoming data. This is documented behavior.

evidence.claim: Make only processes incoming webhook payloads when the associated scenario is active

diagnostic_signals: Webhook queue shows pending payloads but execution history is empty
Scenario toggle is OFF
audit_notes: Core behavior well documented. Scenario must be active is a fundamental Make requirement.

title: Webhook queue is full — Make returns HTTP 400 to sender
problem: Make's webhook queue has a capacity limit. When the queue is full (the scenario cannot process payloads fast enough), Make returns HTTP 400 to the sending service. The payload is rejected and not queued.
symptoms: External service logs show HTTP 400 responses from Make's webhook endpoint
Make webhook queue shows maximum items
Data loss risk — events rejected by a full queue are not stored by Make

likely_causes.cause: The scenario processes payloads slower than the external service sends them, causing queue buildup until the queue is full
A sudden spike in external events overwhelmed the queue capacity

diagnosis_steps: Open Make > Webhooks and check the queue size for the affected webhook
Compare the average scenario execution time with the event dispatch rate from the external service
Identify the processing bottleneck: slow external API calls inside the scenario, complex processing, or rate-limited downstream APIs

solutions.solution: Decouple reception from processing: use a first lean scenario that immediately stores the payload in a Make Data Store, then a second scheduled scenario processes the stored payloads. This keeps the reception scenario fast and prevents queue buildup.
solutions.conditions: When the scenario processing is inherently slow — the recommended architecture for high-volume webhooks

solutions.solution: Optimize the scenario execution time by removing unnecessary modules, batching API calls, and reducing synchronous external API calls
solutions.conditions: When the processing time can be reduced sufficiently to match the incoming event rate

prevention: Design webhook receiver scenarios to execute as fast as possible — ideally under 5 seconds
Separate payload reception (fast) from payload processing (slow) using the Data Store intermediate pattern
Monitor webhook queue size during high-traffic periods

origin_details.evidence: Make documentation states that when the webhook queue is full, Make returns HTTP 400 to the sender. The queue capacity is documented.

evidence.claim: Make returns HTTP 400 to the webhook sender when the webhook queue is full

conditions: Event rate exceeds scenario processing speed

diagnostic_signals: External service shows 400 responses from Make webhook endpoint
Make webhook queue at or near capacity
Scenario execution time is high relative to event frequency
[observed message variant] "Make returns HTTP 400 to the webhook sender when the queue is full"
audit_notes:
HTTP 400 on full queue is documented in Make Help Center. Queue capacity limit is documented but the specific value may vary by plan — not included to avoid stale data.

title: Webhook endpoint rate limited — Make returns HTTP 429 to sender
problem: The external service sends webhook events to Make at a rate exceeding Make's per-webhook request limit. Make returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) to the sender. Events above the limit are rejected.
symptoms: External service delivery logs show HTTP 429 responses from Make's webhook endpoint
Some events are missing from Make processing — the rejected events were not queued
429 pattern correlates with high-frequency event bursts from the external service

likely_causes.cause: The external service is sending webhook events faster than Make's per-webhook rate limit allows

diagnosis_steps: Check the external service's webhook delivery log for 429 responses
Check Make's documentation for the current per-webhook rate limit
Measure the actual event dispatch rate from the external service

solutions.solution: Configure the external service to throttle its webhook dispatch rate to stay within Make's documented per-webhook limit
solutions.conditions: When the external service supports configurable dispatch rates

solutions.solution: Use the external service's event batching feature if available — group multiple events into a single webhook payload rather than one request per event
solutions.conditions: When the external service supports event batching

prevention: Before integrating a high-volume event source, verify the event dispatch rate against Make's webhook rate limits
Prefer event batching over individual event webhooks for high-volume sources

origin_details.evidence: Make documentation states a per-webhook request rate limit exists and returns 429 when exceeded.

evidence.claim: Make returns HTTP 429 to webhook senders that exceed Make's per-webhook request rate limit

conditions: Event dispatch rate exceeds Make webhook rate limit

diagnostic_signals: External service shows 429 responses from Make webhook endpoint
Events are missing from Make despite being dispatched
Event bursts correlate with 429 pattern
[observed message variant] "Make returns HTTP 429 when the per-webhook rate limit is exceeded"
audit_notes:
429 rate limiting for webhooks is documented in Make Help Center. Specific rate limit values are plan-dependent and not included to avoid stale figures.

title: Inactive webhook returns HTTP 410 Gone — webhook expired
problem: Make webhooks that have not received any event for an extended period may be deactivated by Make. The webhook URL returns HTTP 410 Gone to senders, indicating the webhook is no longer active. The associated scenario stops receiving events.
symptoms: External service delivery logs show HTTP 410 responses from the Make webhook URL
Scenario has not received any webhook events for an extended period
The webhook no longer appears as 'Listening' in Make

likely_causes.cause: The Make webhook was deactivated due to prolonged inactivity — Make expires webhooks that receive no events for an extended period

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make > Webhooks and check whether the webhook is still active
Check the scenario status — it may have been deactivated
Verify whether the external service has been sending events to this webhook recently

solutions.solution: Reactivate the scenario and the webhook in Make. Update the webhook URL in the external service if it has changed.
solutions.conditions: When the webhook was deactivated due to inactivity

prevention: Monitor scenarios using webhooks to ensure they receive events regularly
Set up a Make scenario failure notification to detect when webhook scenarios stop receiving events

origin_details.evidence: Make documentation states that webhooks inactive for an extended period return 410 Gone.

evidence.claim: Make returns HTTP 410 Gone when a webhook has been deactivated due to inactivity

sequence: webhook receives no events for extended period
conditions: Webhook inactive for Make's inactivity threshold

diagnostic_signals: External service shows 410 responses from Make webhook URL
Scenario has no recent webhook executions
Webhook not visible or inactive in Make > Webhooks
[observed message variant] "Make returns HTTP 410 Gone when the webhook is deactivated due to inactivity"
audit_notes:
410 for inactive webhooks is documented in Make Help Center. The specific inactivity threshold is not included as it may vary by plan or change. Confidence 0.80 — core behavior documented, specific threshold unconfirmed.

title: Webhook Response module returns response before processing completes
problem: Make's 'Webhooks > Respond to a Webhook' module sends an HTTP response to the webhook sender immediately when executed. If placed late in the scenario, the sender may time out waiting. If placed at the beginning, subsequent modules can still fail without the sender knowing — the scenario and the response are decoupled.
symptoms: External service reports webhook delivery timeout even though Make eventually processes the event
The Respond to Webhook module is placed at the end of a long scenario
Sender receives a 200 but data is missing because processing failed after the response was sent

likely_causes.cause: The Respond to Webhook module is placed too late in the scenario — the sender's timeout expires before Make sends the response
The Respond to Webhook module is placed at the beginning — it sends 200 immediately, but subsequent modules fail silently from the sender's perspective

diagnosis_steps: Check the position of the 'Respond to a Webhook' module in the scenario
Check the external service's webhook timeout value
Measure the total scenario execution time in the execution history
Determine whether the sender needs confirmation of successful processing or only acknowledgment of receipt

solutions.solution: Place the 'Respond to a Webhook' module immediately after the trigger (as the first module) to send an instant acknowledgment, then continue processing. Add an Error Handler to notify on failure separately.
solutions.conditions: When the external service has a short timeout and needs a fast acknowledgment — most common pattern

solutions.solution: Place the 'Respond to a Webhook' module at the end of the scenario if the sender needs confirmation that processing succeeded, and ensure the entire scenario runs within the sender's timeout
solutions.conditions: When the sender requires confirmation of successful end-to-end processing and the scenario is fast enough

prevention: Default to placing Respond to Webhook early in the scenario for most use cases
Always check the sender's webhook timeout before designing the response position

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Respond to a Webhook
origin_details.evidence: The Respond to a Webhook module and its positioning relative to processing is documented in Make Help Center.

evidence.claim: Make's 'Respond to a Webhook' module sends the HTTP response immediately when executed in the scenario flow

conditions: Response position determines when sender receives acknowledgment

diagnostic_signals: External service shows webhook delivery timeout
Respond to Webhook module is positioned late in a long scenario
Sender receives 200 but data is missing or incorrect
audit_notes: Respond to Webhook module is documented in Make Help Center. The behavior of immediate response on execution is confirmed. Positioning guidance is derived from Make documentation and widely confirmed in community.

title: Webhook payload cannot be parsed — body type mismatch
problem: Make receives a webhook payload but cannot parse it into structured fields because the webhook module's body type setting does not match the actual format of the incoming payload. Downstream mapping is empty.
symptoms: Webhook module receives data but all downstream field mappings are empty or unavailable
Bundle inspector shows the payload as a single raw text field instead of structured fields
Scenario runs but no data flows to downstream modules correctly

likely_causes.cause: Webhook body type is set to 'Raw' when the incoming payload is JSON — no automatic field parsing occurs
Webhook body type is set to 'JSON' when the payload is form-encoded (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)

diagnosis_steps: Open the webhook module settings and check the body type (JSON / Form Data / Raw / Multipart Form Data)
Trigger a test event and inspect the raw payload received
Check the Content-Type header of the incoming request to determine the actual format
Compare the configured body type with the actual content type

solutions.solution: Change the webhook body type to match the incoming payload format: 'JSON' for application/json payloads, 'Form Data' for form-encoded payloads
solutions.conditions: When the body type setting does not match the actual payload format

solutions.solution: If body type must remain 'Raw', add the JSON module's Parse JSON action immediately after the webhook to parse the body string into structured fields
solutions.conditions: When Raw is required and the payload is JSON

prevention: Check the Content-Type of the incoming webhook before setting the body type in Make
Send a test event during setup and inspect the raw payload before building downstream mappings

origin_details.evidence: Webhook body type settings (JSON, Form Data, Raw, Multipart) are documented in Make Help Center.

evidence.claim: Make webhook body type settings (JSON, Form Data, Raw, Multipart Form Data) determine how the incoming payload is parsed into bundle fields

conditions: Body type setting does not match actual payload Content-Type

diagnostic_signals: Downstream mapping panel shows no structured fields after webhook
Bundle inspector shows single raw text field
Scenario runs but output is empty or null
audit_notes: Body type settings confirmed in Make documentation. Merged and improved from previous webhook-payload-invalid entry.
